faq.q: Is it my fault my parents split up?
faq.a: No, never. Parents separate because of grown-up problems between them. Nothing you did or said caused it, and nothing you do can fix it, because it is not your job.
asks: Is it my fault my parents are splitting up?
Did I make my parents divorce?

faq.q: How do I get used to two homes?
faq.a: Keep a calendar so you know where you will be, have some favourite things in each home, and tell your parents what helps you feel settled.
asks: Tell me about the Two homes

faq.q: Who can I talk to about my family changing?
faq.a: Either parent, a grandparent, a teacher, a school counsellor or another trusted adult. Talking helps your feelings feel smaller.
asks: Tell me about the Talk to a parent

faq.q: Will my parents still love me?
faq.a: Yes. Parents stop being partners, but they never stop being your parents. Their love for you does not change.
asks: Do my parents still love me?

faq.q: Is it okay to feel angry about it?
faq.a: Yes. Sad, angry, worried, even relieved: all feelings are okay. Tell someone how you feel instead of keeping it inside.

facts: Child psychologists say children often wrongly blame themselves when parents separate, so it helps to hear clearly that it is not their fault.
Many children live in two homes, and routines like a shared calendar help them feel settled.
